title: Applied ML experiment scratchpad - 2026-03-07 (Asha)
content:
Context:
- Quick scratchpad for local eval runs and quantization notes. Goal: find lowest-cost quantization profile for redwood-13B-like family that keeps chat-quality > baseline on prompt_set_chat_v2.
- Tests to run this week: 4-bit QAT-ish profile (smooth-clip), int8 dynamic, 3-bit experimental (if perf allows).

Recent runs (local deduped logs):
- run_id: ash-20260307-01
  model: redwood-13B-quant-4bit-smooth-clip
  config: 4-bit GPTQ-like, per-channel scale, K/V cache enabled, no fp16 fallback
  dataset: prompt_set_chat_v2 (200 prompts, mix of instruction, long-context, tool-calls)
  metrics: automated (bleu-ish/rouge not ideal for chat), human proxy: accept_rate=0.82 (n=50 quick checks)
  perf: p50 latency (1-token stream) = 115ms on T4-small local sim, tokens/sec = 210 (batch=4)
  notes: hallucination on knowledge questions increased vs baseline (~+7%). Good conversationality for short prompts.

- run_id: ash-20260307-02
  model: redwood-13B-int8-dynamic
  config: int8 dynamic, per-tensor, fallback fp16 for attention matmul
  dataset: same
  metrics: accept_rate=0.87 (n=50 quick checks)
  perf: p50 latency = 95ms, tokens/sec = 260 (batch=4)
  notes: much closer to baseline on knowledge, some edge-case tokenization artifacts.

Preliminary takeaways:
- int8 dynamic looks promising as a first step: lower latency and better quality than 4-bit smooth-clip on these prompts.
- 4-bit has cost advantage on throughput but regression on knowledge QA; need to try QAT or mixed precision for attention layers.
- Need to add targeted evals for tool-calling and JSON-structured responses - current automated metrics miss structural errors.

Immediate TODOs (prioritized):
- [ ] run focused eval: 150 prompts for tool-calling & json-output correctness (metric: strict-parse-rate) - target >95%
- [ ] try hybrid quant profile: 4-bit for FFN, int8 for attention kernels (ash-20260307-hybrid)
- [ ] instrument trace for KV cache hit ratio and recopies (why 4-bit shows worse knowledge?)
- [ ] add small human eval batch (n=60) for baseline vs int8 vs 4-bit to quantify accept_rate with blind labeling
- [ ] open PR with config templates for int8 dynamic and hybrid profile (link above)

Notes on prompting and eval harness:
- prompt_set_chat_v2: includes: instruction prompts (short), chain-of-thought style, long-context (2k tokens), tool-call stubs. Need to split into subsets for fine-grained regressions.
- For hallucination detection: create focused QA subset (50 items) pulled from internal knowledge base; check precise fact-match.
- For JSON/tool outputs: create a parser script that returns pass/fail + error type (schema, missing fields, extra fields). Add to harness.

Commands I ran (local):
- python run_eval.py --model redwood-13B-int8-dynamic --prompts data/prompt_set_chat_v2.json --batch 4 --max-tokens 512 --out results/ash-20260307-02.json
- python quant_inspect.py results/ash-20260307-02.json --check-structural-errors

Questions / open experiments to coordinate with Jamie/Jordan:
- Should we prioritize int8 dynamic for Dedicated config (predictable throughput) or aim to push 4-bit with QAT for cost? (cc Jamie for Dedicated perf numbers)
- Can SRE help run hybrid profile at larger scale (64 batch) to estimate cost curve? Links: /confluence ML-EVALS-2026 -> cost model doc.

Scratch notes (ideas):
- Maybe run a short-canary A/B on Dedicated: route 10% traffic to int8 dynamic vs 90% baseline to measure real-world accept_rate and latency percentiles.
- Consider building a tiny eval-annotation UI to get blind labels from TPMs (quick turnaround).

Quick log of changes to configs (to commit):
- quant_profiles/int8-dynamic.yaml -> tuned per-tensor fallback for attention
- quant_profiles/4bit-smooth-clip.yaml -> reduced clip threshold from 2.5 -> 2.0 after initial run (re-run needed)

Next sync: quick standup sync with Jamie at 11:30 (today) - confirm which runs they can kick off on infra pool.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc light. Move polished summary + human eval table to Confluence after we have final numbers.
